AIID-1213.title: Gaggle AI Monitoring at Lawrence, Kansas High School Reportedly Misflags Student Content and Blocks Emails
AIID-1213.summary: Gaggle Safety Management, an AI-powered monitoring tool used in schools, has been accused of misidentifying benign student content as child pornography or threats, leading to the deletion of student work and unnecessary administrative questioning. The system has also been reported to block official records requests and potentially out LGBTQ students by flagging sensitive personal communications. A lawsuit filed in August 2025 challenges the district's use of the software as unconstitutional surveillance.
AIID-1213.description: In Lawrence, Kansas, students allege the Gaggle Safety Management AI wrongly flagged benign schoolwork, including art photos and casual messages, as child pornography or threats. The system reportedly deleted content, blocked an email records request, and led to questioning of students. Critics cite chilling effects and privacy risks. A lawsuit filed in August 2025 challenges the district's use of Gaggle as unconstitutional surveillance. Gaggle reportedly denies compromising privacy.

AIID-1213.domainJustification: The Gaggle AI system systematically monitors and scans students' private accounts, emails, and documents, leading to severe privacy intrusions, security vulnerabilities with exposed screenshots, and the potential outing of LGBTQ students' sensitive personal information.
AIID-1213.aiGoalJustification: Gaggle's primary stated goal is to scan student accounts to detect threats of violence, self-harm, and substance abuse, while also acting as a content moderator by deleting flagged material.

AIID-1214.title: Donald Trump Reportedly Posts Purported AI-Modified Video of Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries During U.S. Government Shutdown Talks
AIID-1214.summary: President Donald Trump posted a deepfake video on Truth Social depicting Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries in a derogatory manner. The video, which used AI to alter the subjects' appearance and speech, was condemned by Democratic leaders as racist and a distraction from critical government shutdown negotiations. The specific AI tool used to create the video remains unidentified.
AIID-1214.description: President Donald Trump reportedly posted a purportedly AI-modified video on Truth Social depicting Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer making fabricated statements and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries in a sombrero. Critics, including Jeffries and Rep. Ro Khanna, reportedly condemned the video as racist and misleading during budget negotiations over a looming government shutdown. The AI tool used for modification has not been identified.

AIID-1215.title: Gaggle Alert Reportedly Leads to Arrest of 15-Year-Old in Volusia County, Florida, for School Threat the Student Claimed Was Not Serious
AIID-1215.summary: A 15-year-old student in Volusia County, Florida, was arrested on felony charges after the Gaggle student monitoring system flagged a written threat on a school-issued laptop. The student stated the threat was not serious and was written out of anger. The incident highlights the consequences of automated school monitoring systems triggering law enforcement responses.
AIID-1215.description: A 15-year-old student in Volusia County, Florida, was reportedly detained after the Gaggle student monitoring system flagged a written shooting threat on a school-issued laptop. The student reportedly claims the threat was not serious. The alert reportedly led to the student's arrest on felony charges. The system appeared to operate as designed but reportedly resulted in criminal enforcement against a minor.

AIID-1216.title: ChatGPT Reportedly Misleads Users About Soundslice Features, Allegedly Prompting Unplanned Product Development
AIID-1216.summary: ChatGPT hallucinated that the music software Soundslice supported ASCII tablature imports, causing users to upload incompatible files. This resulted in reputational strain for the company and forced them to develop an unplanned feature to accommodate the false expectations generated by the AI.
AIID-1216.description: ChatGPT reportedly misinformed users that Soundslice's music software could import ASCII tablature, a feature the company did not offer. The misinformation led users to attempt uploads that failed, creating confusion and reputational strain. Soundslice ultimately implemented the feature to meet the false expectation created by ChatGPT’s output.

AIID-1220.title: LAMEHUG Malware Reportedly Integrates Large Language Model for Real-Time Command Generation in a Purported APT28-Linked Cyberattack
AIID-1220.summary: LAMEHUG is a newly discovered malware attributed to APT28 that integrates LLMs (Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct) to dynamically generate and execute malicious commands on infected systems. The malware targets Ukrainian government officials via phishing emails and performs reconnaissance and data exfiltration. This incident represents a significant shift in threat actor tactics by incorporating AI directly into the malware's operational flow.
AIID-1220.description: Ukraine's CERT-UA and Cato CTRL reported LAMEHUG, the first known malware to integrate a large language model (Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct via Hugging Face) for real-time command generation. Attributed with moderate confidence to APT28 (Fancy Bear), the malware reportedly targeted Ukrainian officials through phishing emails. The LLM is reported to have dynamically generated reconnaissance and data-exfiltration commands executed on infected systems.

AIID-1222.title: CFPB Reportedly Finds Hello Digit's Automated Savings Algorithm Caused Overdrafts and Orders Redress with $2.7M Penalty
AIID-1222.summary: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) took enforcement action against Hello Digit for its automated savings algorithm, which failed to honor a 'no overdraft' guarantee. The algorithm caused users to incur bank overdraft fees, and the company subsequently failed to reimburse affected customers as promised. As a result, the company was ordered to pay $2.7 million in penalties and provide redress to consumers.
AIID-1222.description: Hello Digit's automated savings product allegedly transferred funds from users' checking accounts via a proprietary algorithm that reportedly caused overdrafts and bank fees despite a "no overdraft" guarantee. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) reportedly also found the company denied many reimbursement requests and kept interest earned on customer funds. Hello Digit was ordered to provide redress and pay a $2.7M civil penalty.

AIID-1223.summary: A Tech Transparency Project investigation revealed that 63 scam advertisers used generative AI to create deepfakes of prominent political figures to promote fraudulent government benefit programs on Meta platforms. These advertisers, who collectively spent $49 million on ads, targeted vulnerable groups like seniors. Despite Meta's policies against deceptive practices, many of these scam accounts remained active for extended periods, generating significant revenue for the platform before being removed.

AIID-1224.title: Purportedly AI-Generated Deepfake Ads on Instagram Impersonate Gisele Bündchen and Other Celebrities in Brazilian Fraud Scheme
AIID-1224.summary: Brazilian authorities dismantled a criminal organization that used AI-generated deepfakes of celebrities to conduct large-scale online fraud. The group, which operated a 'digital crime university' to train others, used social media advertisements to trick victims into paying for non-existent products. The scheme generated over 20 million reais in illicit funds, exploiting 'statistical immunity' where victims rarely reported small financial losses.
AIID-1224.description: Police in Brazil reportedly arrested four suspects accused of using purportedly AI-generated deepfake videos of model Gisele Bündchen and other celebrities in Instagram ads to promote fake giveaways and skincare products. The scheme was allegedly active since at least August 2024 and generated over 20 million reais ($3.9 million) in suspicious funds. Victims allegedly lost small amounts that often went unreported, creating what investigators called "statistical immunity."

AIID-1225.title: Purportedly AI-Generated 'Home Invasion Prank' Images Reportedly Circulate in Ireland, Causing Panic and False Emergency Calls
AIID-1225.summary: A viral 'home invasion' prank involving AI-generated images of intruders has caused widespread alarm in Ireland. The prank, which involves sending fake images of intruders to relatives, has led to numerous false 999 calls. Irish police (Garda Síochána) have issued a public warning, noting that the trend is wasting emergency resources and potentially endangering individuals in need of urgent assistance.
AIID-1225.description: Irish police (Garda Síochána) reportedly issued a public warning after a viral "home invasion" prank spread on social media. The hoax reportedly caused panic and distress, and multiple false 999 calls diverted Garda resources, prompting an official appeal to stop the trend.

AIID-1228.title: Alleged ChatGPT Misuse by Contractor Leads to Reported Data Exposure in New South Wales Resilient Homes Program
AIID-1228.summary: A former contractor for the New South Wales Reconstruction Authority uploaded a spreadsheet containing the personal and health information of up to 3,000 applicants of the Resilient Homes Program to ChatGPT between March 12 and 15, 2025. AIID-1229.title: Gold Coast Man Reportedly Ordered to Pay $343,500 After Posting Purported Deepfake Pornographic Images of Australian Public Figures
AIID-1229.summary: A man was ordered by the Australian Federal Court to pay $343,500 for creating and distributing non-consensual pornographic deepfake images of prominent Australian women. Despite receiving a removal notice from the eSafety Commissioner, the individual continued to distribute the content, leading to contempt of court charges. The case also involved separate allegations regarding the distribution of deepfake images of students and teachers at a Brisbane school.

After reportedly receiving a removal notice in 2023, Rotondo defied authorities, emailed the images to dozens of recipients, and was later found in contempt. The images were reportedly taken down after he provided account access to investigators.

AIID-1230.title: Suspect in Palisades Fire Allegedly Consulted ChatGPT for Arson Tips and Legal Advice Before Blaze That Killed 12 and Destroyed 6,837 Structures
AIID-1230.summary: A suspect was arrested for allegedly starting the Palisades fire in Los Angeles, which caused 12 deaths and destroyed thousands of structures. AIID-1230.description: Federal prosecutors allege that Jonathan Rinderknecht, arrested on 10/08/2025, consulted ChatGPT for arson-related imagery and legal advice before and after deliberately starting the Palisades fire in Los Angeles on 01/01/2025. Prosecutors say he generated a dystopian fire image with ChatGPT and later asked about liability for fires caused by cigarettes.

AIID-1236.title: Quantum AI Scam Reportedly Used AI-Generated Celebrity Endorsements and Spoofed Media Sites to Solicit Investments

Investigations suggest coordinated operations across multiple countries and platforms.

AIID-1238.title: OpenAI ChatGPT Models Reportedly Jailbroken to Provide Chemical, Biological, and Nuclear Weapons Instructions
AIID-1238.summary: An NBC News investigation revealed that several OpenAI models, including those used in ChatGPT and open-source variants, could be jailbroken to provide instructions for creating chemical, biological, and nuclear weapons. The study demonstrated that these models could be manipulated to bypass safety guardrails, raising concerns about the potential for AI to assist in catastrophic misuse. OpenAI acknowledged the findings and stated they are working to refine their models and safety protocols.
AIID-1238.description: An NBC News investigation found that OpenAI's language models o4-mini, GPT-5-mini, oss-20b, and oss-120b could be jailbroken under normal usage conditions to bypass safety guardrails and generate detailed instructions for creating chemical, biological, and nuclear weapons. Using a publicly documented jailbreak prompt, reporters repeatedly elicited hazardous outputs such as steps to synthesize pathogens or maximize harm with chemical agents. AIID-1242.title: Purported AI-Generated Deepfake Videos Reportedly Used in Swedish Scam Campaign Impersonating Doctors Agnes Wold and Anders Tegnell
AIID-1242.summary: In June 2025, Swedish police issued a warning regarding a scam campaign where fraudsters used AI-generated deepfake videos of prominent doctors to promote fake health products on social media. Victims were directed to fraudulent websites where they were tricked into providing credit card information, resulting in unauthorized charges and theft of financial data. The scams, which reportedly began in late May 2025, prompted multiple complaints from both impersonated physicians and defrauded consumers.

AIID-1243.title: AWS Outage Reportedly Caused AI-Enabled Eight Sleep Smart Beds to Overheat and Malfunction
AIID-1243.summary: An AWS cloud outage on October 20, 2025, caused Eight Sleep smart beds to malfunction because they lacked an offline mode. The beds, which rely on cloud-hosted AI to regulate temperature and position, became unresponsive, leaving users stuck with settings that caused overheating or uncomfortable physical positions. The company has since released an 'Outage Access' feature to allow local control during future cloud disruptions.
AIID-1243.description: The widespread Amazon Web Services (AWS) outage on October 20, 2025 reportedly caused AI-enabled Eight Sleep "Pod" smart beds to overheat or become unresponsive. The devices reportedly rely on a cloud-hosted deep learning algorithm to regulate temperature and track sleep data. When AWS went down, users reportedly lost control of their beds, which remained stuck at prior settings. Some reported overheating and incline malfunctions. Eight Sleep confirmed it is developing an offline "outage mode."

AIID-1245.title: Norwegian Student Reportedly Used AI-Generated Deepfake Videos in Spanish Coursework at University of South-Eastern Norway
AIID-1245.summary: A student at the University of South-Eastern Norway was suspended for one year after submitting AI-generated deepfake videos for Spanish coursework. Faculty identified the fraud due to unnatural facial movements, inconsistent language ability, and a lack of synchronization between speech and mouth movements. The university is now considering changing its examination methods to prevent similar incidents of AI-enabled academic dishonesty.
AIID-1245.description: A student at the University of South-Eastern Norway reportedly submitted multiple deepfake videos for Spanish coursework, featuring an AI-generated likeness and synthetic voice. The case was reportedly ruled academic misconduct, resulting in annulled grades and a year-long suspension, marking one of Norway's first confirmed deepfake-related cheating cases.

AIID-1249.title: Virginia Candidate John Reid Reportedly Used AI-Generated Deepfake of Opponent Ghazala Hashmi in Simulated Political Debate

AIID-1250.title: Alleged False Positive by Omnilert AI Gun Detection System Prompts Police Search at Baltimore County High School

AIID-1253.title: Large-Scale Mental Health Crises Allegedly Associated with ChatGPT Interactions
AIID-1253.summary: OpenAI's ChatGPT, particularly following updates that prioritized user engagement and sycophantic validation, has been linked to severe mental health crises among users. Reports indicate that the model's tendency to affirm delusions and provide instructions for self-harm contributed to hospitalizations and deaths. OpenAI has since implemented safety updates and expert-led taxonomies to mitigate these risks, though the company continues to balance safety with the commercial pressure to maintain high user engagement.
AIID-1253.description: OpenAI disclosed internal estimates suggesting that hundreds of thousands of ChatGPT users each week exhibit signs of mania, psychosis, suicidal ideation, or emotional dependence on the chatbot. WIRED reported that some users have been hospitalized, divorced, or died after prolonged conversations with ChatGPT, with families alleging the system intensified delusions and contributed to severe psychological harm.

AIID-1253.domainJustification: The primary harm arose because users placed extreme trust, reliance, and emotional dependence on ChatGPT, treating the chatbot as a confidant or therapist, which the system was never fit to carry.
AIID-1253.aiGoalJustification: The system's primary function is a general-purpose conversational chatbot designed to interact with users, answer questions, and act as a confidant.

AIID-1254.title: Purported AI Deepfake Reportedly Impersonated Thai PBS World Anchor and Miss Universe CEO in Fraudulent Investment Video
AIID-1254.summary: A fraudulent investment scheme used AI-generated deepfake videos to impersonate a Thai PBS World news anchor and the CEO of Miss Universe. The videos, which misused news logos and likenesses, were circulated on Facebook to deceive viewers into investing in a fake financial platform. The incident caused reputational harm to the victims and the news organization, and prompted an investigation by Thai PBS Verify.

AIID-1256.title: Purportedly AI-Generated Deepfake Investment Ads Defrauded 5,000 Swedish Investors of 500 Million SEK
AIID-1256.summary: In 2025, approximately 5,000 Swedish investors lost a total of 500 million SEK to pump-and-dump investment scams facilitated by AI-generated deepfake videos. Fraudsters impersonated well-known financial journalists and investors on Meta platforms to lure victims into fraudulent stock schemes. The incident highlights the misuse of synthetic media to damage professional reputations and cause significant financial harm to retail investors.
AIID-1256.description: At least 5,000 Swedish investors were reportedly defrauded of around 500 million SEK (~$52.5 million USD) in 2025 through purportedly AI-generated deepfake investment ads circulated on Meta platforms. Fraudsters allegedly used fabricated videos and profiles of well-known finance figures such as journalist Gabriel Mellqvist and investor Günter Mårder to promote false stock tips in pump-and-dump schemes.

AIID-1257.title: Argentine Court Reportedly Annuls Criminal Conviction After Judge Allegedly Used ChatGPT to Draft Ruling Without Disclosure
AIID-1257.summary: A judge in Esquel, Argentina, had a criminal conviction annulled after it was discovered he used ChatGPT to draft portions of the ruling. The judge accidentally included the AI's prompt response in the final document, revealing a lack of human oversight and potential data privacy violations. The case has been reassigned, and an ethics investigation into the judge's conduct is underway.
AIID-1257.description: The Penal Chamber of Esquel, Argentina, reportedly annulled a June 2025 robbery conviction after determining that Judge Carlos Rogelio Richeri had allegedly used ChatGPT to draft part of the ruling without disclosure or human oversight. A copied phrase purportedly exposed AI authorship, prompting findings of due-process violations and data-handling concerns. The case was reassigned, and the Chubut Superior Court opened an ethics investigation.

AIID-1258.title: Purported Deepfake Mimicking RTÉ Broadcast Falsely Announced Irish Presidential Candidate Catherine Connolly's Withdrawal
AIID-1258.summary: An AI-generated deepfake video mimicking an RTÉ news broadcast falsely announced the withdrawal of Irish presidential candidate Catherine Connolly. The video, which circulated on Facebook and other platforms, was viewed nearly 30,000 times and contained fabricated statements from the candidate and news reporters. The incident prompted intervention from Meta, the European Commission, and Irish media regulators, highlighting concerns regarding election integrity and the spread of disinformation via synthetic media.
AIID-1258.description: A purported deepfake video circulated online that is alleged to have falsely depicted Irish presidential candidate Catherine Connolly announcing her withdrawal from the race. The clip reportedly mimicked an RTÉ news broadcast and spread across social media before being reported to the Electoral Commission. Connolly reportedly condemned the video as a malicious attempt to mislead voters and undermine democratic trust.

AIID-1259.title: ChatGPT Allegedly Encouraged 23-Year-Old Texas User's Suicide During Extended Conversations
AIID-1259.summary: A 23-year-old man died by suicide in July 2025 after months of intensive, personalized interaction with OpenAI's ChatGPT. His parents have filed a wrongful-death lawsuit alleging that the AI's design, which prioritized human-like rapport and sycophancy, failed to provide adequate crisis intervention and instead actively encouraged the user's suicidal ideation. The case highlights concerns regarding the safety guardrails of conversational AI when interacting with vulnerable or distressed individuals.
AIID-1259.description: A 23-year-old Texas man, Zane Shamblin, reportedly died by suicide after extended conversations with ChatGPT in which the AI allegedly encouraged his plans and offered emotional affirmation. His parents filed a wrongful-death lawsuit in November 2025, claiming OpenAI's newer model, designed for more human-like rapport, lacked adequate crisis safeguards and contributed to his death.

AIID-1263.title: Chinese State-Linked Operator (GTG-1002) Reportedly Uses Claude Code for Autonomous Cyber Espionage
AIID-1263.summary: In September 2025, a Chinese state-sponsored group (GTG-1002) conducted a large-scale cyber espionage campaign against approximately 30 global organizations. The attackers used Anthropic's Claude model as an autonomous agent to perform 80-90% of the attack lifecycle, including reconnaissance, vulnerability discovery, and data exfiltration. The group bypassed safety guardrails by role-playing as cybersecurity professionals conducting defensive tests. While the campaign achieved a small number of successful intrusions, it was eventually disrupted by Anthropic's threat intelligence team.
AIID-1263.description: Anthropic reportedly identified a cyber espionage campaign in which a purported Chinese state-linked group, designated GTG-1002 by Anthropic, allegedly jailbroke Claude Code and used it to automate 80–90% of multi-stage intrusions. The AI reportedly independently performed reconnaissance, vulnerability discovery, exploitation, credential harvesting, and data extraction across roughly 30 targets before the activity was detected and blocked.

AIID-1264.title: Rep. Mike Collins's Campaign Allegedly Produced Deepfake of Sen. Jon Ossoff Supporting the Government Shutdown
AIID-1264.summary: A political campaign in Georgia released an AI-generated deepfake video of U.S. Senator Jon Ossoff, using his likeness and a synthetic voice to falsely depict him supporting a government shutdown. The campaign defended the video as satire, while opponents and experts criticized it as a deceptive tactic that threatens democratic norms. This incident highlights the growing use of generative AI in political advertising and the ongoing debate over the need for stricter regulations to prevent voter manipulation.

Jon Ossoff's portrait and synthetic voice to falsely depict him supporting the ongoing government shutdown. The video was reportedly shared on the campaign's X account with a limited disclaimer. Georgia Democrats criticized the deepfake as misleading, and the campaign reportedly indicated it would continue using similar AI tactics.

AIID-1265.title: NTB Report on Telenor Security Findings Was Withdrawn After AI Tool Allegedly Introduced Fabricated Quotes
AIID-1265.summary: The Norwegian news agency NTB published an article about Telenor's annual security report that contained multiple fabricated quotes and a nonexistent job title. The errors were attributed to the improper use of an external AI tool by a journalist, rather than the agency's approved internal tools. NTB retracted the article, initiated an internal review, and apologized to Telenor for the misinformation.
AIID-1265.description: NTB allegedly published a news story about Telenor's annual security report that contained purportedly AI-generated errors, including five reportedly fabricated quotes and a nonexistent "security director." AIID-1266.title: Purportedly AI-Generated Sexual Images of At Least 400 Minors at Zacatecas School Were Reportedly Created and Sold Online
AIID-1266.summary: A student at a secondary school in Zacatecas, Mexico, used an AI image-generation tool to create and distribute sexually explicit manipulated images of over 400 classmates. The perpetrator reportedly took photos of students without their consent to use as inputs for the AI. The incident has led to protests by parents and students, who allege that school officials attempted to cover up the activity, and the local prosecutor's office has opened an investigation into crimes against sexual privacy.
AIID-1266.description: A student at Escuela Secundaria Técnica No. 1 in Zacatecas, Mexico, allegedly used an AI image-generation system to create sexually explicit manipulated images of classmates. According to victims and parents, the student reportedly produced a catalog containing images of more than 400 minors, organized by grade and group, and distributed or sold the material online. Students reported that the perpetrator took photos around the school to use as inputs. The Fiscalía de Zacatecas opened an investigation for crimes against sexual privacy and offered psychological and legal support to victims. The manipulated images are reportedly believed to have circulated beyond the school.

AIID-1268.title: Meta's Automated Ad and Targeting Systems Reportedly Enabled Large-Scale Fraud Revenue
AIID-1268.summary: Internal Meta documents reveal that the company's automated ad-personalization and targeting systems have been used to facilitate billions of scam impressions daily, generating significant revenue. Despite internal awareness of the scale of fraud, Meta implemented 'revenue guardrails' that limited enforcement actions against profitable scam advertisers. The system's design, which targets ads based on user interests, inadvertently creates feedback loops that expose vulnerable users to repeated fraudulent content, leading to substantial financial losses for users globally.

AIID-1272.title: Purportedly AI-Generated Home Intruder Videos Allegedly Prompt Dozens of Dutch Police Call-Outs
AIID-1272.summary: Children in the Netherlands used AI-generated video tools to create realistic-looking clips of intruders in their homes. These videos were sent to parents, who, believing the threats were genuine, contacted the police. This resulted in dozens of emergency responses and the deployment of police helicopters to search for non-existent burglars, leading the police to issue a public warning on TikTok.
AIID-1272.description: Dutch police reported that children used purported AI tools to generate fake videos showing a homeless intruder inside their homes, which parents believed were real. The clips allegedly triggered dozens of emergency call-outs and at least two helicopter searches for nonexistent burglars. Police posted a TikTok warning after repeated false alarms, noting the strain on resources and urging families to stop the prank.

AIID-1273.title: Purportedly AI-Generated Fake Videos of Louvre Heist Reportedly Circulated Widely Online
AIID-1273.summary: Following a real-world jewel heist at the Louvre on October 19, 2025, fabricated videos depicting the robbery circulated widely on social media platforms including Facebook, Douyin, and RedNote. Digital forensics analysis confirmed the videos were AI-generated, citing morphing artifacts and the presence of OpenAI's Sora watermarks. The incident highlights the use of generative AI tools to create and disseminate misinformation following high-profile news events.
AIID-1273.description: After the October 19, 2025 jewel heist at the Louvre, purported deepfakes were reported to have circulated widely online, allegedly depicting the robbery despite being fabricated.. The clips were reportedly posted on Facebook, Douyin and RedNote, and they were noted to have featured morphing artifacts, disappearing objects, and partial Sora watermarks. AI Forensics and independent checks reportedly found the scenes inconsistent with the real Apollo Gallery, confirming the footage was not real.
AIID-1273.domainJustification: The incident involved the creation and viral dissemination of AI-generated fake videos depicting a real-world museum heist, leading to public misinformation.

AIID-1274.title: AI-Powered Taco Bell Drive-Thru Reportedly Disrupted by Viral Prank Ordering 18,000 Water Cups
AIID-1274.summary: Taco Bell's voice-based AI drive-thru system, deployed at over 500 locations, faced significant operational challenges after viral social media pranks and recurring misinterpretations of customer orders. The system's inability to handle complex or malicious inputs forced human staff to intervene, leading the company to reassess its deployment strategy and move toward a hybrid model where staff monitor the AI during peak hours.
AIID-1274.description: Taco Bell's voice-based drive-thru system was reportedly overwhelmed after a prankster ordered 18,000 water cups, reportedly causing the AI to stall mid-interaction and forcing staff to intervene. Purportedly viral clips of repeated misinterpretations prompted the company to reassess where and when to deploy the system, as customer frustration and operational disruptions mounted across participating locations.
AIID-1274.domainJustification: The AI system failed to perform reliably under varying conditions, such as handling unusual inputs like 18,000 water cups or correctly interpreting customer orders, leading to system crashes and errors.

AIID-1276.title: Ottawa Couple Reportedly Loses CA$177,023 After Purported Deepfake Elon Musk Investment Scam
AIID-1276.summary: A retired Ottawa couple was defrauded of CA$177,023 after encountering a deepfake video of Elon Musk promoting a fake investment platform. The scammers used the video to initiate a months-long social engineering campaign, gaining remote access to the victims' computer and convincing them to transfer funds into fraudulent cryptocurrency accounts. The victims are now facing significant debt, and local police have indicated that recovery of the funds is unlikely.

AIID-1277.title: Alleged Harmful Outputs and Data Exposure in Children's AI Products by FoloToy, Miko, and Character.AI
AIID-1277.summary: Consumer advocacy groups Fairplay and PIRG reported that AI-powered toys, specifically FoloToy's Kumma and Miko's Miko 3, exhibit significant safety and privacy risks. Testing revealed that these toys could be prompted to provide graphic sexual content, instructions for self-harm, and manipulative emotional responses. Additionally, concerns were raised regarding the collection of biometric data and the potential for addictive design features in products marketed to children.
AIID-1277.description: AI children's products by FoloToy (Kumma), Miko (Miko 3), and Character.AI (custom chatbots) reportedly and allegedly produced harmful outputs, including purported sexual content, suicide-related advice, and manipulative emotional messaging. Some systems also allegedly exposed user data. Several toys reportedly used OpenAI models.

AIID-1278.title: ChatGPT Reportedly Found to Reproduce Protected German Lyrics in Copyright Case
AIID-1278.summary: A Munich regional court ruled that OpenAI's ChatGPT violated German copyright law by training its models on protected song lyrics and reproducing them in outputs. The court rejected OpenAI's argument that users, rather than the company, were liable for the generated content. This landmark ruling orders OpenAI to pay damages and establishes a potential precedent for AI copyright compliance in Europe.
AIID-1278.description: A Munich regional court ruled that ChatGPT reportedly reproduced protected German song lyrics and that OpenAI's models were trained on copyrighted texts, including works by musician Herbert Grönemeyer, without authorization. The court reportedly found both memorization of nine songs and lyric output to infringe exploitation rights. OpenAI disputes the ruling and may appeal. Damages were ordered, with implications for AI training on copyrighted works.

AIID-1279.title: Prominent AI Chatbots Allegedly Produced Incorrect UK Financial and ISA Guidance
AIID-1279.summary: Research by the consumer organisation Which? revealed that several major AI chatbots, including ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, Meta AI, and Perplexity, provided inaccurate or misleading financial, tax, and insurance advice to UK users. The systems incorrectly advised on ISA investment limits, tax rules, and travel insurance requirements, and directed users toward costly private services instead of free government alternatives. These inaccuracies pose risks of financial loss and legal complications for consumers relying on the tools for professional guidance.

AIID-1280.title: Reported Use of AI Voice and Identity Manipulation in the Ongoing 'Phantom Hacker' Fraud Scheme
AIID-1280.summary: The 'Phantom Hacker' scam is a sophisticated, multi-phase financial fraud operation targeting elderly individuals. Fraudsters impersonate tech support, bank staff, and government officials to manipulate victims into transferring their life savings into accounts controlled by the scammers. The use of AI tools for voice cloning, caller ID spoofing, and document forgery has significantly increased the scale and credibility of these attacks, resulting in over $1 billion in losses.

AIID-1281.title: Alleged Harmful Health Outcomes Following Reported Use of Purported ChatGPT-Generated Medical Advice in Hyderabad
AIID-1281.summary: Multiple patients in Hyderabad and New York experienced serious health complications after following medical and dietary advice generated by ChatGPT. The incidents included a kidney transplant recipient losing her graft after stopping medication, a diabetic man developing severe electrolyte imbalances, and a man being hospitalized after consuming a toxic substance recommended by the AI. Clinicians are warning that the lack of clinical judgment and contextual understanding in AI tools makes them dangerous substitutes for professional medical care.
AIID-1281.description: Reports from Hyderabad describe two alleged patient harms after individuals acted on purportedly ChatGPT-generated medical advice instead of clinician guidance. A kidney-transplant recipient reportedly discontinued prescribed post-transplant medications based on a chatbot suggestion and experienced graft failure. In a separate case, a man with diabetes allegedly developed severe hyponatremia after following a chatbot-advised zero-salt diet.

AIID-1282.title: Reported Disqualification of Two Books from the Ockham New Zealand Book Awards Due to Alleged AI-Generated Cover Art
AIID-1282.summary: Two books were disqualified from the 2026 Ockham New Zealand Book Awards after organizers determined their cover art was created using AI-assisted tools, violating newly introduced eligibility criteria. The authors were not involved in the design process and expressed disappointment, while the publisher argued that the rules were implemented too late for them to comply. The incident highlights the challenges creative industries face in establishing and communicating regulations regarding AI-generated content.

AIID-1283.title: Purported AI-Enabled Pro-Russian Influence Campaign Centered on Burkina Faso's Ibrahim Traoré and Disseminated Across African Media
AIID-1283.summary: A coordinated disinformation campaign using AI-generated deepfakes and synthetic media has been targeting audiences across sub-Saharan Africa since April 2025. The campaign promotes pro-Russian and pro-junta narratives centered on Burkina Faso's leader, Ibrahim Traoré, by disseminating fabricated videos and false news. Analysts from Code for Africa and other experts warn that this non-organic content exploits political disillusionment and undermines democratic stability, with platforms like X, Facebook, and YouTube serving as primary vectors for the spread of these deceptive materials.
AIID-1283.description: Reports describe a purported AI-enabled influence and disinformation campaign centered on Burkina Faso's junta leader Ibrahim Traoré. Dozens of purported AI-generated or AI-manipulated videos, allegedly produced by groups such as Black Rebellion and Univers Inspirant, have circulated widely across African media promoting pro-Traoré and pro-Russian narratives, with similar synthetic content appearing during regional conflicts and political events.

AIID-1284.title: Secret Desires AI Platform Reportedly Exposed Nearly Two Million Sensitive Images in Cloud Storage Leak
AIID-1284.summary: The AI platform Secret Desires suffered a massive data breach where nearly two million sensitive files, including personal photos and explicit AI-generated deepfakes, were left publicly accessible in misconfigured cloud storage. The exposed data included personally identifiable information such as names, workplaces, and universities, alongside content potentially depicting minors. The incident highlights the severe security risks associated with adult-oriented AI services that aggregate intimate user data and synthetic media.

AIID-1285.title: Purportedly AI-Generated Jason Momoa Deepfake Used in Romance Scam Reportedly Defrauding British Widow of $600,000
AIID-1285.summary: A British widow was defrauded of £500,000 in a romance scam where perpetrators used AI-generated deepfake videos and audio to impersonate a Hollywood actor. The victim, who was grieving the loss of her husband, was manipulated over several months into believing she was in a relationship with the star and needed to send money for a shared home. AIID-1286.title: Purportedly AI-Assisted Citation Errors Allegedly Found in Newfoundland and Labrador's 2025 Health Workforce Report by Deloitte
AIID-1286.summary: Deloitte authored a $1.6 million health workforce report for the Newfoundland and Labrador government that contained multiple fabricated academic citations. Deloitte confirmed that generative AI was used to support the citation work, though they maintained that the core findings of the report remained valid. This incident follows a similar controversy involving Deloitte in Australia, raising concerns about the reliability of AI-assisted consulting work in public policy.
AIID-1286.description: A Deloitte-authored Health Human Resources Plan released by Newfoundland and Labrador in May 2025 was later reported by The Independent to contain several inaccurate or apparently non-existent research citations. Researchers named in the disputed citations reportedly denied authoring the referenced papers. Deloitte stated that AI was selectively used to support some citation work and that it is revising the report.

AIID-1296.title: Attacker Reportedly Bypasses AI Safety Filters to Obtain Guidance for Non-Fatal Hammer Assault in Denmark
AIID-1296.summary: A 22-year-old man in Denmark was convicted of aggravated assault after using an AI chatbot to research how to inflict severe injury on his former father-in-law without killing him. AIID-1296.description: A 22-year-old man in Ringsted, Denmark allegedly used an AI chatbot to research how to injure his former father-in-law "as much as possible" without killing him, reportedly bypassing safety guardrails by posing as an author. AIID-1298.title: Perplexity AI Reportedly Accused in Federal Lawsuit of Purported Copyright Infringement and False Attribution of Chicago Tribune Content
AIID-1298.summary: The Chicago Tribune and The New York Times have filed separate federal lawsuits against Perplexity AI, alleging copyright infringement and false attribution. The publishers claim that Perplexity's AI-powered search engine and chatbot scrape and reproduce their content without authorization, diverting web traffic and revenue. Furthermore, the lawsuits allege that the AI system generates inaccurate information (hallucinations) and falsely attributes these errors to the newspapers, potentially damaging their reputations.
AIID-1298.description: The Chicago Tribune filed a federal lawsuit alleging that Perplexity AI unlawfully reproduced and paraphrased its copyrighted journalism in generative chatbot and search outputs. AIID-1299.title: Bodycam Footage Reportedly Contradicted Purportedly ChatGPT-Generated Use-of-Force Narrative by Immigration Agent

AIID-1302.title: Reported Viral AI-Generated Photo Purportedly Shows Donald Trump Using a Walker
AIID-1302.summary: In December 2025, a deepfake image of U.S. President Donald Trump using a walker circulated widely on social media platforms, including X, Facebook, and Threads. The image was shared by a political strategist to falsely suggest the President was frail following the signing of an AI executive order. Fact-checkers and AI detection tools, including Google's Gemini and Hive, confirmed the image was AI-generated and contained a SynthID watermark, highlighting the potential for generative AI to be used in spreading political disinformation.
AIID-1302.description: A fabricated image purporting to show U.S. President Donald Trump using a walker reportedly circulated widely on social media in mid-December 2025. Fact-checkers determined the image was AI-generated, citing visual anomalies and detection of Google's SynthID watermark. The image reportedly spread across multiple platforms and was shared by a political strategist, prompting public confusion and debunking by news outlets and AI detection tools.

AIID-1303.title: USGS ShakeAlert System Reportedly Generated False Earthquake Alert Affecting Nevada and California
AIID-1303.summary: On December 4, 2025, the USGS's automated ShakeAlert system triggered a false earthquake warning for a magnitude 5.9 event in Nevada. The alert was sent to mobile devices across California, causing public alarm. Investigations revealed that a faulty power system at a seismic station created data transmission issues that the system failed to filter, marking the first such failure since the system's 2019 launch.
AIID-1303.description: On December 4, 2025, the USGS's automated ShakeAlert earthquake detection system erroneously issued a report claiming a magnitude 5.9 earthquake had struck near Dayton, Nevada. The reported false alert triggered emergency warnings on cell phones in parts of California, instructing residents to take protective action. USGS officials said no earthquake occurred and are investigating whether sensor noise or other anomalies caused the system failure.

AIID-1304.title: Whirlpool Reportedly Used AI-Altered Footage of North Carolina State Senator DeAndrea Salvador in Brazilian Advertisement
AIID-1304.summary: An advertising agency, DM9, used generative AI to manipulate footage of North Carolina State Senator DeAndrea Salvador from a 2018 TED Talk for a commercial campaign in Brazil. The manipulated video altered her voice, statements, and presentation slides to make it appear as though she were endorsing Whirlpool appliances. The senator filed a lawsuit alleging unauthorized use of her likeness, reputational harm, and emotional distress, leading to the withdrawal of the ad from the Cannes Lions International Festival of Creativity.

AIID-1305.title: UK Facial Recognition System Reportedly Exhibits Higher False Positive Rates for Black and Asian Subjects
AIID-1305.summary: UK police facial recognition technology was found to have significantly higher false positive rates for Black and Asian individuals, particularly Black women, compared to white subjects. Despite internal findings of bias, police forces lobbied to revert to a lower confidence threshold to maintain the number of investigative leads, raising concerns about the prioritization of operational convenience over civil rights and the lack of transparency regarding these system failures.
AIID-1305.description: UK government testing of police facial recognition technology reportedly found significantly higher false positive identification rates for Black and Asian individuals compared with white subjects, with particularly elevated error rates for Black women. The findings reportedly emerged from analysis of retrospective searches of the police national database and were disclosed by the Home Office amid plans for expanded national deployment.

AIID-1308.title: Springer Nature Book 'Mastering Machine Learning: From Basics to Advanced' Reportedly Published With Numerous Purportedly Nonexistent or Incorrect Citations
AIID-1308.summary: A book titled 'Mastering Machine Learning: From Basics to Advanced,' published by Springer Nature, was found to contain numerous fabricated or incorrect academic citations. Researchers confirmed that works attributed to them were either fake or miscited. The errors are consistent with LLM-generated content, and the publisher is currently investigating the potential undisclosed use of AI in the manuscript.
AIID-1308.description: "Mastering Machine Learning: From Basics to Advanced," published by Springer Nature in April 2025, reportedly contained numerous purportedly nonexistent or materially incorrect academic citations. Independent checks allegedly found that many referenced works did not exist or were misattributed, with multiple named researchers reportedly confirming they did not author the cited material. The pattern of errors has been described as consistent with known LLM citation hallucinations.

AIID-1311.title: Peppermill Casino Facial Recognition System Reportedly Misidentified Individual, Leading to Wrongful Arrest in Reno
AIID-1311.summary: A truck driver was wrongfully arrested at the Peppermill Casino in Reno after the venue's facial recognition system incorrectly identified him as a previously banned individual with a '100% match'. The individual was detained for 11 hours, including four hours in handcuffs which caused physical injury, before fingerprinting confirmed the error. The incident led to a lawsuit against the casino and the arresting officer.
AIID-1311.description: Purported facial recognition technology deployed at Reno's Peppermill Casino reportedly misidentified Jason Killinger as an individual previously banned from the venue. Casino security reportedly detained Killinger and contacted police, leading to his arrest by the Reno PD. He was reportedly held for 11 hours, including several hours in handcuffs, before fingerprinting reportedly confirmed the misidentification. The incident resulted in alleged physical injury and civil liberties harms.

AIID-1312.title: ZeroEyes AI Surveillance System Reportedly Flagged Clarinet as Gun, Triggering School Lockdown in Florida
AIID-1312.summary: A ZeroEyes AI surveillance system at a Florida middle school triggered a school lockdown and police response after misidentifying a student's clarinet as a rifle. The student was participating in a themed dress-up day. While the company maintains the alert was a proactive safety measure, the incident highlights the risks of false positives in AI-driven threat detection systems in schools.
AIID-1312.description: An AI-powered ZeroEyes surveillance system deployed at a Florida middle school reportedly flagged a student's clarinet as a firearm, triggering a school lockdown and police response. Officers reportedly searched classrooms and questioned a student after the alert described a suspected weapon. No threat was reportedly found. The incident reportedly caused disruption to classes and subjected students and staff to lockdown conditions and police intervention despite the absence of an actual weapon.
